memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Receive the atonement money from the Israelites and use it for the service of the tent of meeting. It will be a memorial for the Israelites before the Lord, making atonement for your lives." - Exodus 30:16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The atonement money was not stored away; it went into the service of the tent of meeting. Every person's half shekel became part of the structure where God met His people. And God calls it a memorial — a lasting reminder before Him of those who had been counted and covered.

Each contribution was small. Half a shekel from one individual would accomplish nothing on its own. But together, these small payments funded the place where the whole nation met with God. What seemed insignificant individually became substantial collectively.

That is how God's work has always been built. Jesus watched a widow put in two tiny coins and said she had given more than all the wealthy donors (Mark 12:41-44). God does not measure the way we do. Your small faithfulness, your modest giving, your unremarkable service — these are not lost. They are gathered into something larger and remembered before God. Nothing given to Him disappears.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I dismiss my contribution as too small to matter?
What small faithfulness could I offer, trusting God to gather it into something larger?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You gather small offerings into great purposes and remember every one. Help me give and serve faithfully, trusting that nothing offered to You is ever wasted. Amen.
